{"id": "771d4ce3-1058-416d-9f6a-c9926a50a487", "role": "user", "content": [{"id": "tooluse_N5CtuHx0hzBVBhTFcmFVPf", "content": "[{'text': '## Documentation search results\\n\\n{\"content\":{\"result\":[{\"rank_order\":1,\"title\":\"Automated network incident response with AWS DevOps Agent | Networking & Content Delivery\",\"context\":\"## Scenario 4: Bedrock Interface Endpoint subnets removed, AI feature breaks\\\\n\\\\nThe Bedrock Runtime Interface Endpoint (`simulated-workload-Bedrock-Endpoint`) creates ENIs in two private subnets. Private DNS resolves `bedrock-runtime.us-east-1.amazonaws.com` to those ENI IP addresses. The following Figure 21 shows the removal of subnet association.\\\\n\\\\n*[](https://d2908q01vomqb2.cloudfront.net/5b384ce32d8cdef02bc3a139d4cac0a22bb029e8/2026/04/17/NetCDNBlog-1723-image-21.gif)Figure 21: Modify subnets associated with interface VPC endpoint*\\\\n\\\\nWhen someone removes both subnet associations, the ENIs are deleted. The endpoint still exists and Private DNS still resolves the hostname to the endpoint, but there is nothing to handle the traffic. This is the scenario that is particularly hard to spot by hand, because the console still shows the endpoint as \u201cAvailable\u201d even though requests time out with no response. It is worth noting the difference between the two endpoint types: VPC Gateway Endpoints (Amazon S3, Amazon DynamoDB) work through route table entries and endpoint policies, so a misconfiguration there returns an Access Denied (HTTP 403 Forbidden) error. Interface VPC Endpoints (Amazon Bedrock and many other AWS services) work through ENIs in your subnets with their own security groups, so when those ENIs are gone, you get connection timeouts instead. But the database still works (VPC local route), Amazon S3 still works (VPC Gateway Endpoint has its own route table entry), and outbound internet connectivity still works (NAT Gateway route is intact). Only the Bedrock AI check turns red.\\\\n\\\\n[](https://d2908q01vomqb2.cloudfront.net/5b384ce32d8cdef02bc3a139d4cac0a22bb029e8/2026/04/17/NetCDNBlog-1723-image-22.png)*Figure 22: Simulated workload application status page*\\\\n\\\\nDevOps Agent receives the `BedrockAccessFailures` alarm and investigates:\\\\n\\\\n1. **Checks endpoint configuration** \u2013 Finds zero subnet associations on the Interface VPC Endpoint.\\\\n2. **Searches CloudTrail logs** \u2013 Finds the `ModifyVpcEndpoint` API call, including who removed the subnet associations\\\\n\\\\n*[truncated \u2014 additional content omitted]*\",\"url\":\"https://aws.amazon.com/blogs/networking-and-content-delivery/automated-network-incident-response-with-aws-devops-agent/\"},{\"rank_order\":2,\"title\":\"How PayU built a secure enterprise AI assistant using Amazon Bedrock | Artificial Intelligence\",\"context\":\"## Private access to foundation models\\\\n\\\\nGiven that our organizational data was included as context in prompts sent to Amazon Bedrock and the generated responses could contain sensitive information, we needed a robust solution to help prevent exposure of this data to the public internet. Our goal was to establish a secure data perimeter that would help mitigate potential risks associated with internet-facing communication. To achieve this, we implemented AWS PrivateLink, creating a private and dedicated connection between our VPC and Amazon Bedrock. With this configuration, Amazon Bedrock is accessible as though it resides within our own VPC, removing the need for an internet gateway or NAT gateway. By setting up an interface endpoint with PrivateLink, we provisioned a network interface directly in our VPC subnet, so that data remains securely within the AWS network. This architecture not only strengthens our security posture by minimizing external exposure but also streamlines connectivity for our internal applications.\\\\n\\\\nThe following diagram illustrates this architecture.\\\\n\\\\n[](https://d2908q01vomqb2.cloudfront.net/f1f836cb4ea6efb2a0b1b99f41ad8b103eff4b59/2025/07/08/ml-19011-bedrock_private_connection.png)\",\"url\":\"https://aws.amazon.com/blogs/machine-learning/how-payu-built-a-secure-enterprise-ai-assistant-using-amazon-bedrock/\"},{\"rank_order\":3,\"title\":\"Use AWS PrivateLink to set up private access to Amazon Bedrock | Artificial Intelligence\",\"context\":\"## Set up the VPC endpoint for Amazon Bedrock\\\\n\\\\nIn this section, we use Amazon Virtual Private Cloud (Amazon VPC) to set up the VPC endpoint for Amazon Bedrock to facilitate private connectivity from your VPC to Amazon Bedrock.\\\\n\\\\n1. On the Amazon VPC console, under **Virtual private cloud** in the navigation pane, choose **Endpoints**.\\\\n2. Choose **Create endpoint**.\\\\n\\\\n3. For **Name tag**, enter `bedrock-vpce`.\\\\n4. Under **Services**, search for bedrock-runtime and select `com.amazonaws.<region>.bedrock-runtime`.\\\\n5. For **VPC**, specify the VPC `Bedrock-GenAI-Project-vpc` that you created through the CloudFormation stack in the previous section.\\\\n\\\\n6. In the **Subnets** section, and select the Availability Zones and choose the corresponding subnet IDs from the drop-down menu.\\\\n\\\\n7. For **Security groups**, select the security group with the group name `Bedrock-GenAI-Stack-VPCEndpointSecurityGroup-` and description `Allow TLS for VPC Endpoint`.\\\\n\\\\nA security group acts as a virtual firewall for your instance to control inbound and outbound traffic. Note that this VPC endpoint security group only allows traffic originating from the security group attached to your VPC private subnets, adding a layer of protection.\\\\n\\\\n8. Choose **Create endpoint**.\\\\n9. In the **Policy** section, select **Custom** and enter the following least privilege policy to ensure only certain actions are allowed on the specified foundation model resource, `arn:aws:bedrock:*::foundation-model/anthropic.claude-instant-v1` for a given principal (such as Lambda function IAM role).\\\\n\\\\n ```\\\\n {\\\\n \\\\t\\\\\"Version\\\\\": \\\\\"2012-10-17\\\\\",\\\\n \\\\t\\\\\"Statement\\\\\": [\\\\n \\\\t\\\\t{\\\\n \\\\t\\\\t \\\\\"Action\\\\\": [\\\\n \\\\t\\\\t \\\\\"bedrock:InvokeModel\\\\\"\\\\n \\\\t\\\\t ],\\\\n \\\\t\\\\t \\\\\"Resource\\\\\": [\\\\n \\\\t\\\\t \\\\\"arn:aws:bedrock:*::foundation-model/anthropic.claude-instant-v1\\\\\"\\\\n \\\\t\\\\t ],\\\\n \\\\t\\\\t \\\\\"Effect\\\\\": \\\\\"Allow\\\\\",\\\\n \\\\t\\\\t \\\\\"Principal\\\\\": {\\\\n \\\\\"AWS\\\\\": \\\\\"arn:aws:iam::<accountid>:role/GenAIStack-Bedrock\\\\\"\\\\n }\\\\n \\\\t\\\\t}\\\\n \\\\t]\\\\n }\\\\n ```\\\\n\\\\nIt may take up to 2 minutes until the interface endpoint is created and the status changes to Available. You can refresh the page to check the latest status\",\"url\":\"https://aws.amazon.com/blogs/machine-learning/use-aws-privatelink-to-set-up-private-access-to-amazon-bedrock/\"},{\"rank_order\":4,\"title\":\"How do I troubleshoot connectivity issues with my Amazon VPC interface endpoints?\",\"context\":\"Short description\\\\n-----------------\\\\n\\\\nTo troubleshoot connectivity issues with your [interface Amazon VPC endpoints](https://docs.aws.amazon.com/vpc/latest/privatelink/create-interface-endpoint.html), use [Amazon VPC Reachability Analyzer](https://repost.aws/knowledge-center/vpc-connectivity-reachability-analyzer), or manually take the following actions:\\\\n\\\\n* Check your DNS name resolution.\\\\n* Check your endpoint policy configuration.\\\\n* Check the configuration of the security group of the endpoint.\\\\n* Check your subnet network access control lists (network ACLs).\\\\n* Check your routing configuration.\\\\n* Check your connectivity to the endpoints.\\\\n* Troubleshoot MTU (Maximum Transmission Unit) issues that cause SSL connection errors.\\\\n\\\\nResolution\\\\n----------\\\\n\\\\nUse [Amazon VPC Reachability Analyzer](https://repost.aws/knowledge-center/vpc-connectivity-reachability-analyzer) to [analyze paths across multiple AWS accounts](https://docs.aws.amazon.com/vpc/latest/reachability/multi-account.html) in your organization, and check for security group, network ACL, and route table configurations. For more information, see [How Reachability Analyzer works](https://docs.aws.amazon.com/vpc/latest/reachability/how-reachability-analyzer-works.html).\\\\n\\\\n**Note:** Use Amazon Q to [enhance Amazon VPC network troubleshooting](https://aws.amazon.com/blogs/networking-and-content-delivery/introducing-amazon-q-support-for-network-troubleshooting/) and diagnose connectivity issues with natural language queries.\\\\n\\\\nIf reachability analyzer doesn\\'t resolve your connectivity issue, then manually troubleshoot your configuration\",\"url\":\"https://repost.aws/knowledge-center/vpc-fix-gateway-or-interface-endpoint\"},{\"rank_order\":5,\"title\":\"Use interface VPC endpoints (AWS PrivateLink) to create a private connection between your VPC and Amazon Bedrock\",\"context\":\"## Connect to Amazon Bedrock through your VPC endpoint\\\\n\\\\nAfter you create your VPC endpoint, you can route Amazon Bedrock API calls through it. How you do this depends on whether you enabled private DNS for the endpoint.\\\\n\\\\n* **Private DNS enabled** \u2013 No code changes needed. All Amazon Bedrock API calls from within the VPC automatically route through the endpoint using the standard service DNS names (e.g., `bedrock-runtime.region.amazonaws.com`).\\\\n* **Private DNS not enabled** \u2013 You must explicitly specify the VPC endpoint URL in your API calls, as shown in the following examples.\\\\n\\\\n**AWS CLI**\\\\n\\\\nUse the `--endpoint-url` flag to route requests through your VPC endpoint:\\\\n\\\\n```\\\\naws bedrock-runtime invoke-model \\\\\\\\\\\\n --model-id anthropic.claude-sonnet-4-6-v1 \\\\\\\\\\\\n --body \\'{\\\\\"anthropic_version\\\\\": \\\\\"bedrock-2023-05-31\\\\\", \\\\\"max_tokens\\\\\": 1024, \\\\\"messages\\\\\": [{\\\\\"role\\\\\": \\\\\"user\\\\\", \\\\\"content\\\\\": \\\\\"Hello\\\\\"}]}\\' \\\\\\\\\\\\n --cli-binary-format raw-in-base64-out \\\\\\\\\\\\n --endpoint-url https://vpce-id.bedrock-runtime.region.vpce.amazonaws.com \\\\\\\\\\\\n output.json\\\\n```\\\\n\\\\n**Python (boto3)**\\\\n\\\\nPass the `endpoint_url` parameter when creating the client. This approach works for AWS Lambda functions and any application using the AWS SDK:\\\\n\\\\n```\\\\nimport boto3\\\\n\\\\nclient = boto3.client(\\\\n \\\\\"bedrock-runtime\\\\\",\\\\n region_name=\\\\\"us-east-1\\\\\",\\\\n endpoint_url=\\\\\"https://vpce-id.bedrock-runtime.us-east-1.vpce.amazonaws.com\\\\\"\\\\n)\\\\n\\\\nresponse = client.converse(\\\\n modelId=\\\\\"anthropic.claude-sonnet-4-6-v1\\\\\",\\\\n messages=[{\\\\\"role\\\\\": \\\\\"user\\\\\", \\\\\"content\\\\\": [{\\\\\"text\\\\\": \\\\\"Hello\\\\\"}]}]\\\\n)\\\\n```\\\\n\\\\nReplace `vpce-id` with your VPC endpoint ID (e.g., `vpce-029dea71225152fde`). You can find this ID in the VPC console under **Endpoints**\",\"url\":\"https://docs.aws.amazon.com/bedrock/latest/userguide/vpc-interface-endpoints.html\"}]}}\\n\\n## Recent AWS announcements (What\\'s New)\\n\\nNewer than your training data may be. When these conflict with the documentation results above or with what you remember, prefer the most recent dated source.\\n\\n{\"content\":{\"result\":[{\"rank_order\":1,\"title\":\"connecting-vpcs-with-peering\",\"skill_description\":\"Establishes VPC peering connections between two VPCs for direct private network connectivity. Always use this skill when creating or managing VPC peering \u2014 it validates CIDR overlap, updates all route tables in both VPCs, configures DNS resolution, and provides security group guidance that are critical for correct connectivity.\\\\n\\\\nServices: ec2, vpc\\\\nTasks: configure, deploy\\\\nPersona: developer, devops\\\\nWorkload: networking\\\\n*\",\"skill_name\":\"connecting-vpcs-with-peering\"},{\"rank_order\":2,\"title\":\"configuring-vpc-endpoints-for-private-aws-service-access\",\"skill_description\":\"Configures VPC endpoints (interface and gateway) for private AWS service access using AWS PrivateLink. Use when setting up secure private connectivity to S3, DynamoDB, and other AWS services without internet gateway, NAT device, or public IP addresses. Covers endpoint creation, security groups, route tables, and DNS configuration.\\\\n\\\\nServices: ec2, vpc, s3, dynamodb\\\\nTasks: configure\\\\nPersona: developer, devops\\\\nWorkload: networking\\\\n*\",\"skill_name\":\"configuring-vpc-endpoints-for-private-aws-service-access\"},{\"rank_order\":3,\"title\":\"Amazon Bedrock AgentCore Runtime, Browser, and Code Interpreter add support for VPC, AWS PrivateLink, CloudFormation, and tagging - AWS\",\"context\":\"Amazon Bedrock has expanded the capabilities of its AgentCore Runtime, Browser, and Code Interpreter services. These enhancements include support for Amazon Virtual Private Cloud (VPC), AWS PrivateLink, AWS CloudFormation, and resource tagging. With VPC connectivity, AgentCore services can securely access private resources within a VPC without internet exposure. AWS PrivateLink provides a private connection between a VPC and Amazon Bedrock AgentCore services. CloudFormation support enables automated resource provisioning through infrastructure as code. Use when deploying multi-AZ VPC infrastructure with automatic CIDR planning and DNS resolution.\\\\n\\\\nServices: ec2, vpc\\\\nTasks: create, configure\\\\nPersona: developer, devops\\\\nWorkload: networking\\\\n*\",\"skill_name\":\"creating-production-vpc-multi-az\"}]}}'}]", "status": "success", "type": "tool_result"}], "created_at": null}
